_comment: Passages a person decided, on top of the ones the tools measured. Nothing regenerates
this file.
{ map, element, cell, gfx, type, skill, toMap, toCell }   declare or re-point one
{ map, element, remove: true }                            take one out
THE ASTRAL PLANE. The four arches of the Well of Dreams map and the way back from
Draconiros' room. They are not neighbours on the world grid - (0,0) and (1,-1) with
nothing between them - so without these the room is placed and unreachable, which for a
player is the same as not being there.
Every number is measured in the capture 'entrar a suenos-hablar con draconiros...':
the jss f11 gives the element, its uid and its skill; the iwo says which one the client
presses; the jru gives the destination map and the jss after it the landing cell. Four
round trips, and all four arches land on the same cell 381, all four returns on 221.
The skill is 184 and NOT the 20739-20743 of the iwo: those are instance uids. Reading
one as the other is what left the well unclickable, with no error anywhere.
THE KANOJEDO OF THE AMAKNA VILLAGE. The door of 88212247 into 99090957, 'The Kanojedo'.
The element is measured: the jss of 88212247 declares 472901 with skill 184 and the map
data puts it on cell 315, one step from where the guardian of the kanojedo stands (316).
The two doors out - 504555 and 504556, landing on 343 - were already in Giny's catalogue;
the way IN was in nobody's. The landing cell 457 is NOT measured: no capture walks through
this door. It is the walkable cell between the two doors out, so whoever comes in stands
where whoever goes out starts from.
THE GM PRISON. Its three maps, all at [66,6] in subarea 751 and joined by nothing on the
world grid, made into one round: the sky jail -> the dungeon -> the island -> the jail.
Where Ankama's own server sends them is not in the client and no capture goes there, so
the round is ours; what each end hangs off is the client's map data (bundle world_401):
105121026, the sky jail. Its one stair: the trapdoor 479454 in the middle of the
corridor, gfx 19649, drawn over cells 300, 314, 315 and 328. Down it goes to the
dungeon, landing on 370 in its big room -- the one with the cage, 92 cells; the 40
behind the bars are walled off from it.
105120002, the dungeon. Not one element on it, so its way out is a FLOOR passage, in
floor_passages.json: the cage hanging from its rope, cell 333, lifts you to the island.
105119744, the island. Its one element is the treasure chest 479462 on cell 300 (gfx
682, the chest's sprite). Opening it puts you back in the jail, on 342 at the foot of
the trapdoor.
Type -1 and skill 184, the pair every measured passage uses (TeleportContent.DefaultType
and DefaultSkill). A prisoner goes through none of them: every passage ends in
TeleportHandler.ToMapAsync, which asks the jail first.
